sanskrit: tatrainam upatiṣṭhanti brāhmaṇā dhanahetavaḥ nādeyaṃ tasya tatkāle kiṃ cid asti dvijātiṣu
english: There brahmins gathered around him seeking wealth; at that time there was nothing he would not give to the twice-born.

sanskrit: tam indro brāhmaṇo bhūtvā bhikṣāṃ dehīty upasthitaḥ svāgataṃ ceti rādheyas tam atha pratyabhāṣata
english: Then Indra, having assumed the form of a brahmin, approached him saying "Give me alms!" And Rādheya (Karṇa) replied to him, "Welcome!"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca devarājam anuprāptaṃ brāhmaṇacchadmanā vṛṣaḥ dṛṣṭvā svāgatam ity āha na bubodhāsya mānasam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the king of the gods arrived in the guise of a brahmin, Vrisha (Karṇa) saw him and said "Welcome!" — but he did not know the intention in his mind.

sanskrit: hiraṇyakaṇṭhīḥ pramadā grāmān vā bahugokulān kiṃ dadānīti taṃ vipram uvācādhirathis tataḥ
english: Then Adhirathi (Karṇa, son of Adhiratha) said to that brahmin: "Shall I give you women adorned with golden necklaces, or villages, or many herds of cattle — what shall I give you?"

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca hiraṇyakaṇṭhyaḥ pramadā yac cānyat prītivardhanam nāhaṃ dattam ihecchāmi tadarthibhyaḥ pradīyatām
english: The brahmin said: "Women with golden necklaces, and whatever else increases joy — I do not wish for such gifts here; let those be given to those who desire them."

sanskrit: yad etat sahajaṃ varma kuṇḍale ca tavānagha etad utkṛtya me dehi yadi satyavrato bhavān
english: "That natural armour and those earrings of yours, O sinless one — cut them off and give them to me, if you are truly committed to your vow of truthfulness."

sanskrit: etad icchāmy ahaṃ kṣipraṃ tvayā dattaṃ paraṃtapa eṣa me sarvalābhānāṃ lābhaḥ paramako mataḥ
english: "This I desire, quickly given by you, O scorcher of foes. This I consider the supreme gain among all gains."

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca avaniṃ pramadā gāś ca nirvāpaṃ bahuvārṣikam tat te vipra pradāsyāmi na tu varma na kuṇḍale
english: Karṇa said: "Land, women, cattle, and ample provisions for many years — all this I will give you, O brahmin, but not the armour, and not the earrings."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ bahuvidhair vākyair yācyamānaḥ sa tu dvijaḥ karṇena bharataśreṣṭha nānyaṃ varam ayācata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Though Karṇa entreated him with many kinds of words, that twice-born asked for no other boon, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: sāntvitaś ca yathāśakti pūjitaś ca yathāvidhi naivānyaṃ sa dvijaśreṣṭhaḥ kāmayām āsa vai varam
english: Though pacified to the best of Karṇa's ability and honoured according to proper rites, that best of twice-born still desired no other boon.

sanskrit: yadā nānyaṃ pravṛṇute varaṃ vai dvijasattamaḥ tadainam abravīd bhūyo rādheyaḥ prahasann iva
english: When that best of twice-born chose no other boon, Rādheya (Karṇa) then spoke to him again, half-smiling:

sanskrit: sahajaṃ varma me vipra kuṇḍale cāmṛtodbhave tenāvadhyo 'smi lokeṣu tato naitad dadāmy aham
english: "My natural armour, O brahmin, and these earrings born of amrita — by these I am invincible in the worlds; therefore I will not give these away."

sanskrit: viśālaṃ pṛthivīrājyaṃ kṣemaṃ nihatakaṇṭakam pratigṛhṇīṣva mattas tvaṃ sādhu brāhmaṇapuṃgava
english: "Accept from me a vast kingdom of the earth, peaceful and free from thorns — please do so, O bull among brahmins."

sanskrit: kuṇḍalābhyāṃ vimukto 'haṃ varmaṇā sahajena ca gamanīyo bhaviṣyāmi śatrūṇāṃ dvijasattama
english: "Freed from the earrings and from the natural armour, I shall become vulnerable to my enemies, O best of twice-born."

sanskrit: yadā nānyaṃ varaṃ vavre bhagavān pākaśāsanaḥ tataḥ prahasya karṇas taṃ punar ity abravīd vacaḥ
english: When the blessed Pākaśāsana (Indra, slayer of Pāka) chose no other boon, Karṇa laughed and then spoke to him these words again:

sanskrit: vidito devadeveśa prāg evāsi mama prabho na tu nyāyyaṃ mayā dātuṃ tava śakra vṛthā varam
english: "You are known to me, O lord of the gods and lord of the divine, O master — it is not right for me to give you a meaningless boon, O Śakra."

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi deveśvaraḥ sākṣāt tvayā deyo varo mama anyeṣāṃ caiva bhūtānām īśvaro hy asi bhūtakṛt
english: "For you are in truth the lord of the gods; it is you who ought to grant a boon to me, for you are the lord and creator of all beings."

sanskrit: yadi dāsyāmi te deva kuṇḍale kavacaṃ tathā vadhyatām upayāsyāmi tvaṃ ca śakrāvahāsyatām
english: "If I give you, O god, both the earrings and the armour, I shall become fit to be slain, and you too, O Śakra, shall be laughed at."

sanskrit: tasmād vinimayaṃ kṛtvā kuṇḍale varma cottamam harasva śakra kāmaṃ me na dadyām aham anyathā
english: "Therefore make an exchange, O Śakra, and take the earrings and the excellent armour — grant me my desire; otherwise I shall not give them."

sanskrit: śakra uvāca vidito 'haṃ raveḥ pūrvam āyann eva tavāntikam tena te sarvam ākhyātam evam etan na saṃśayaḥ
english: Śakra said: "I was recognised — the Sun told you before I even came to you; it is for this reason that everything was revealed to you. This is so, without doubt."

sanskrit: kāmam astu tathā tāta tava karṇa yathecchasi varjayitvā tu me vajraṃ pravṛṇīṣva yad icchasi
english: "So be it as you wish, dear Karṇa — choose whatever you desire, but excepting my thunderbolt, choose what you want."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ karṇaḥ prahṛṣṭas tu upasaṃgamya vāsavam amoghāṃ śaktim abhyetya vavre saṃpūrṇamānasaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Karṇa, greatly delighted, approached Vāsava (Indra) and, going up to the infallible Shakti weapon, chose it with a heart completely satisfied.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca varmaṇā kuṇḍalābhyāṃ ca śaktiṃ me dehi vāsava amoghāṃ śatrusaṃghānāṃ ghātanīṃ pṛtanāmukhe
english: Karṇa said: "In exchange for the armour and the earrings, give me the Shakti, O Vāsava — the infallible one that slays the hosts of enemies on the battlefield."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ saṃcintya manasā muhūrtam iva vāsavaḥ śaktyarthaṃ pṛthivīpāla karṇaṃ vākyam athābravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Vāsava, having reflected in his mind for a moment, O protector of the earth, spoke these words to Karṇa concerning the Shakti:

sanskrit: kuṇḍale me prayacchasva varma caiva śarīrajam gṛhāṇa karṇa śaktiṃ tvam anena samayena me
english: "Give me the earrings and the body-born armour; take from me the Shakti, O Karṇa — but on this condition of mine:"

sanskrit: amoghā hanti śataśaḥ śatrūn mama karacyutā punaś ca pāṇim abhyeti mama daityān vinighnataḥ
english: "The infallible one, when released from my hand, slays enemies by the hundreds and then returns to my hand after I have slain the demons."

sanskrit: seyaṃ tava karaṃ prāpya hatvaikaṃ ripum ūrjitam garjantaṃ pratapantaṃ ca mām evaiṣyati sūtaja
english: "This weapon, once it reaches your hand, after slaying one powerful roaring and blazing enemy, will return to me alone, O son of a charioteer."

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca ekam evāham icchāmi ripuṃ hantuṃ mahāhave garjantaṃ pratapantaṃ ca yato mama bhayaṃ bhavet
english: Karṇa said: "I desire to slay just one enemy in the great battle — one who roars and blazes, from whom there might be fear for me."

sanskrit: indra uvāca ekaṃ haniṣyasi ripuṃ garjantaṃ balinaṃ raṇe tvaṃ tu yaṃ prārthayasy ekaṃ rakṣyate sa mahātmanā
english: Indra said: "You will slay one roaring, powerful enemy in battle; but the one you seek — that one is protected by a great-souled being."

sanskrit: yam āhur vedavidvāṃso varāham ajitaṃ harim nārāyaṇam acintyaṃ ca tena kṛṣṇena rakṣyate
english: "He whom those learned in the Vedas call the Boar, the unconquered Hari, the unthinkable Nārāyaṇa — by that Kṛṣṇa he is protected."

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca evam apy astu bhagavann ekavīravadhe mama amoghā pravarā śaktir yena hanyāṃ pratāpinam
english: Karṇa said: "Even so let it be, O blessed one — for the slaying of one hero, let me have the infallible, supreme Shakti, by which I may slay the blazing one."

sanskrit: utkṛtya tu pradāsyāmi kuṇḍale kavacaṃ ca te nikṛtteṣu ca gātreṣu na me bībhatsatā bhavet
english: "And I shall cut off and give you the earrings and the armour; but when my limbs are cut, may there be no ugliness upon me."

sanskrit: indra uvāca na te bībhatsatā karṇa bhaviṣyati kathaṃ cana vraṇaś cāpi na gātreṣu yas tvaṃ nānṛtam icchasi
english: Indra said: "No ugliness, O Karṇa, will come upon you in any way, nor will there be wounds on your limbs — for you are one who does not desire falsehood."

sanskrit: yādṛśas te pitur varṇas tejaś ca vadatāṃ vara tādṛśenaiva varṇena tvaṃ karṇa bhavitā punaḥ
english: "Such as your father's complexion is, and his radiance, O best among speakers — with that very same complexion, O Karṇa, you shall be again."

sanskrit: vidyamāneṣu śastreṣu yady amoghām asaṃśaye pramatto mokṣyase cāpi tvayy evaiṣā patiṣyati
english: "If, while other weapons are available, you carelessly release the infallible one without need, she will fall back upon you yourself."

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca saṃśayaṃ paramaṃ prāpya vimokṣye vāsavīm imām yathā mām āttha śakra tvaṃ satyam etad bravīmi te
english: Karṇa said: "Only when I face the greatest danger will I release this weapon of Vāsava — as you have told me, O Śakra; this I say to you truly."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ śaktiṃ prajvalitāṃ pratigṛhya viśāṃ pate śastraṃ gṛhītvā niśitaṃ sarvagātrāṇy akṛntata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, having received the blazing Shakti, O lord of the people, Karṇa took up a sharp instrument and cut away all his limbs (of armour).

sanskrit: tato devā mānavā dānavāś ca; nikṛntantaṃ karṇam ātmānam evam dṛṣṭvā sarve siddhasaṃghāś ca nedur; na hy asyāsīd duḥkhajo vai vikāraḥ
english: Then the gods, humans, and demons — all the hosts of Siddhas too — cried out seeing Karṇa cutting himself in this way; for truly there was in him no distress-born change of countenance.

sanskrit: tato divyā dundubhayaḥ praṇeduḥ; papātoccaiḥ puṣpavarṣaṃ ca divyam dṛṣṭvā karṇaṃ śastrasaṃkṛttagātraṃ; muhuś cāpi smayamānaṃ nṛvīram
english: Then divine kettledrums resounded; a divine shower of flowers fell abundantly, seeing Karṇa with his limbs cut by the blade — the hero among men smiling again and again.

sanskrit: tataś chittvā kavacaṃ divyam aṅgāt; tathaivārdraṃ pradadau vāsavāya tathotkṛtya pradadau kuṇḍale te; vaikartanaḥ karmaṇā tena karṇaḥ
english: Then, having cut the divine armour from his body, still wet with blood, he gave it to Vāsava; and having likewise cut off the earrings, he gave them over — by that act Karṇa became known as Vaikartana (the cutter).

sanskrit: tataḥ śakraḥ prahasan vañcayitvā; karṇaṃ loke yaśasā yojayitvā kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ hi mene; tataḥ paścād divam evotpapāta
english: Then Śakra, having deceived Karṇa while smiling, and having joined him to everlasting fame in the world, considered the task of the Pāṇḍavas accomplished — and thereafter flew up to heaven.

sanskrit: śrutvā karṇaṃ muṣitaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrā; dīnāḥ sarve bhagnadarpā ivāsan tāṃ cāvasthāṃ gamitaṃ sūtaputraṃ; śrutvā pārthā jahṛṣuḥ kānanasthāḥ
english: Hearing that Karṇa had been stripped, the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra were all dejected, like men whose pride was broken; but the Pārthas, dwelling in the forest, rejoiced greatly upon hearing of the plight brought upon the son of the charioteer.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kvasthā vīrāḥ pāṇḍavās te babhūvuḥ; kutaś caitac chrutavantaḥ priyaṃ te kiṃ vākārṣur dvādaśe 'bde vyatīte; tan me sarvaṃ bhagavān vyākarotu
english: Janamejaya said: "Where were those heroic Pāṇḍavas at the time? And from whom did they hear this welcome news? What did they do after the twelfth year had passed? Please explain all this to me, revered one."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca labdhvā kṛṣṇāṃ saindhavaṃ drāvayitvā; vipraiḥ sārdhaṃ kāmyakād āśramāt te mārkaṇḍeyāc chrutavantaḥ purāṇaṃ; devarṣīṇāṃ caritaṃ vistareṇa
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: "Having recovered Kṛṣṇa (Draupadī) and routed the Sindhu king, departing from the hermitage of Kāmyaka along with the brahmins, they had heard from Mārkaṇḍeya the ancient tales of the divine seers at length."

sanskrit: pratyājagmuḥ sarathāḥ sānuyātrāḥ; sarvaiḥ sārdhaṃ sūdapaurogavaiś ca tataḥ puṇyaṃ dvaitavanaṃ nṛvīrā; nistīryograṃ vanavāsaṃ samagram
english: They returned with their chariots and retinue, along with all the cooks and foremost attendants; then those heroes among men went to the holy Dvaitavana forest, having endured completely the terrible forest exile.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca evaṃ hṛtāyāṃ kṛṣṇāyāṃ prāpya kleśam anuttamam pratilabhya tataḥ kṛṣṇāṃ kim akurvata pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Janamejaya said: "After Kṛṣṇa (Draupadī) was thus abducted and they had suffered the greatest affliction, and then recovered Kṛṣṇa, what did the Pāṇḍavas do?"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ hṛtāyāṃ kṛṣṇāyāṃ prāpya kleśam anuttamam vihāya kāmyakaṃ rājā saha bhrātṛbhir acyutaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: After Kṛṣṇa was thus abducted and they had suffered the greatest affliction, the steadfast king abandoned Kāmyaka along with his brothers,

sanskrit: punar dvaitavanaṃ ramyam ājagāma yudhiṣṭhiraḥ svādumūlaphalaṃ ramyaṃ mārkaṇḍeyāśramaṃ prati
english: And Yudhiṣṭhira returned again to the beautiful Dvaitavana forest, delightful with sweet roots and fruits, in the direction of the hermitage of Mārkaṇḍeya.

sanskrit: anuguptaphalāhārāḥ sarva eva mitāśanāḥ nyavasan pāṇḍavās tatra kṛṣṇayā saha bhārata
english: Eating fruits gathered from the protected forest, all of them eating in moderation, the Pāṇḍavas dwelt there together with Kṛṣṇa (Draupadī), O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vasan dvaitavane rājā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhīmaseno 'rjunaś caiva mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau
english: Dwelling in Dvaitavana were the king Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Kuntī, Bhīmasena, Arjuna, and the two Pāṇḍava sons of Mādrī,

sanskrit: brāhmaṇārthe parākrāntā dharmātmāno yatavratāḥ kleśam ārchanta vipulaṃ sukhodarkaṃ paraṃtapāḥ
english: Striving on behalf of the brahmins, righteous in soul, firm in their vows — those scorchers of foes endured great suffering that would yield happiness in the end.

sanskrit: ajātaśatrum āsīnaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaṃ vane āgamya brāhmaṇas tūrṇaṃ saṃtapta idam abravīt
english: A brahmin, coming quickly to Ajātaśatru (Yudhiṣṭhira) seated together with his brothers in the forest, and greatly distressed, spoke these words:

sanskrit: araṇīsahitaṃ mahyaṃ samāsaktaṃ vanaspatau mṛgasya gharṣamāṇasya viṣāṇe samasajjata
english: "My fire-kindling sticks (arani), together with my fire-drill, which were hanging on a tree, became entangled in the antlers of a deer rubbing itself against it."

sanskrit: tad ādāya gato rājaṃs tvaramāṇo mahāmṛgaḥ āśramāt tvaritaḥ śīghraṃ plavamāno mahājavaḥ
english: "Taking them, O king, that great deer went off in haste, running swiftly from the hermitage, leaping with great speed."

sanskrit: tasya gatvā padaṃ śīghram āsādya ca mahāmṛgam agnihotraṃ na lupyeta tadānayata pāṇḍavāḥ
english: "Quickly follow its tracks, overtake that great deer, and bring it back so that my fire-sacrifice may not be interrupted — bring them, O Pāṇḍavas!"

sanskrit: brāhmaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā saṃtapto 'tha yudhiṣṭhiraḥ dhanur ādāya kaunteyaḥ prādravad bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
english: Hearing the brahmin's words, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Kuntī, greatly agitated, took up his bow and ran out together with his brothers.

sanskrit: sannaddhā dhanvinaḥ sarve prādravan narapuṃgavāḥ brāhmaṇārthe yatantas te śīghram anvagaman mṛgam
english: All of them, armed and bearing bows, those bulls among men ran forward; striving for the sake of the brahmin, they swiftly gave chase to the deer.

sanskrit: karṇinālīkanārācān utsṛjanto mahārathāḥ nāvidhyan pāṇḍavās tatra paśyanto mṛgam antikāt
english: Though those great warriors let fly karni, nalika, and naraca arrows, the Pāṇḍavas could not strike the deer even as they watched it nearby.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ prayatamānānāṃ nādṛśyata mahāmṛgaḥ apaśyanto mṛgaṃ śrāntā duḥkhaṃ prāptā manasvinaḥ
english: Though they strove hard, that great deer was no longer to be seen; not seeing the deer, those noble-minded ones were exhausted and overcome with sorrow.

sanskrit: śītalacchāyam āsādya nyagrodhaṃ gahane vane kṣutpipāsāparītāṅgāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ samupāviśan
english: Coming to a banyan tree with cool shade in the dense forest, the Pāṇḍavas, their bodies overwhelmed with hunger and thirst, sat down together.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ samupaviṣṭānāṃ nakulo duḥkhitas tadā abravīd bhrātaraṃ jyeṣṭham amarṣāt kurusattama
english: As they were seated there, Nakula, distressed and full of indignation, spoke to his eldest brother, O best of the Kurus:

sanskrit: nāsmin kule jātu mamajja dharmo; na cālasyād arthalopo babhūva anuttarāḥ sarvabhūteṣu bhūyaḥ; saṃprāptāḥ smaḥ saṃśayaṃ kena rājan
english: "Never in this family did dharma sink, nor did wealth become lost through sloth; unsurpassed among all beings even now — how then have we come to this peril, O king?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca nāpadām asti maryādā na nimittaṃ na kāraṇam dharmas tu vibhajaty atra ubhayoḥ puṇyapāpayoḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "There is no boundary to calamities, no fixed sign, no fixed cause; yet dharma distributes here between both merit and sin."

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca prātikāmy anayat kṛṣṇāṃ sabhāyāṃ preṣyavat tadā na mayā nihatas tatra tena prāptāḥ sma saṃśayam
english: Bhīma said: "Pratikamin led Kṛṣṇa (Draupadī) to the assembly hall like a servant — I did not slay him there, and because of that we have come to this peril."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca vācas tīkṣṇāsthibhedinyaḥ sūtaputreṇa bhāṣitāḥ atitīkṣṇā mayā kṣāntās tena prāptāḥ sma saṃśayam
english: Arjuna said: "The words sharp enough to pierce bones spoken by the son of a charioteer (Karṇa) — I endured them though they were exceedingly sharp, and because of that we have come to this peril."

sanskrit: sahadeva uvāca śakunis tvāṃ yadājaiṣīd akṣadyūtena bhārata sa mayā na hatas tatra tena prāptāḥ sma saṃśayam
english: Sahadeva said: "When Śakuni defeated you in the dice game, O Bhārata, I did not slay him there — and because of that we have come to this peril."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā nakulaṃ vākyam abravīt āruhya vṛkṣaṃ mādreya nirīkṣasva diśo daśa
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira spoke these words to Nakula: "Climb a tree, O son of Mādrī, and survey the ten directions."

sanskrit: pānīyam antike paśya vṛkṣān vāpy udakāśrayān ime hi bhrātaraḥ śrāntās tava tāta pipāsitāḥ
english: "Look for water nearby, or trees that grow by water; for these brothers of yours, dear one, are weary and thirsty."

sanskrit: nakulas tu tathety uktvā śīghram āruhya pādapam abravīd bhrātaraṃ jyeṣṭham abhivīkṣya samantataḥ
english: And Nakula, saying "So be it," quickly climbed a tree and, having surveyed all around, spoke to his eldest brother:

sanskrit: paśyāmi bahulān rājan vṛkṣān udakasaṃśrayān sārasānāṃ ca nirhrādam atrodakam asaṃśayam
english: "I see many trees that grow near water, O king, and the calls of cranes; there is certainly water there, without doubt."

sanskrit: tato 'bravīt satyadhṛtiḥ kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ gaccha saumya tataḥ śīghraṃ tūrṇaṃ pānīyam ānaya
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Kuntī, steadfast in truth, said: "Go there quickly, gentle one, and bring water without delay."

sanskrit: nakulas tu tathety uktvā bhrātur jyeṣṭhasya śāsanāt prādravad yatra pānīyaṃ śīghraṃ caivānvapadyata
english: And Nakula, saying "So be it" by the command of his eldest brother, ran to where the water was and quickly reached it.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā vimalaṃ toyaṃ sārasaiḥ parivāritam pātukāmas tato vācam antarikṣāt sa śuśruve
english: He saw the clear water surrounded by cranes and, wishing to drink, then heard a voice from the sky:

sanskrit: mā tāta sāhasaṃ kārṣīr mama pūrvaparigrahaḥ praśnān uktvā tu mādreya tataḥ piba harasva ca
english: "Do not act rashly, dear one — this is my prior possession. First answer my questions, O son of Mādrī, and then drink and take water."

sanskrit: anādṛtya tu tad vākyaṃ nakulaḥ supipāsitaḥ apibac chītalaṃ toyaṃ pītvā ca nipapāta ha
english: But Nakula, disregarding that voice and very thirsty, drank the cool water — and having drunk, he fell down dead.

sanskrit: cirāyamāṇe nakule kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ abravīd bhrātaraṃ vīraṃ sahadevam ariṃdamam
english: When Nakula was long delayed, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Kuntī spoke to his brave brother, the subduer of enemies, Sahadeva:

sanskrit: bhrātā cirāyate tāta sahadeva tavāgrajaḥ taṃ caivānaya sodaryaṃ pānīyaṃ ca tvam ānaya
english: "Your elder brother Nakula is long delayed, dear Sahadeva — bring him, your full brother, and bring water yourself too."

sanskrit: sahadevas tathety uktvā tāṃ diśaṃ pratyapadyata dadarśa ca hataṃ bhūmau bhrātaraṃ nakulaṃ tadā
english: Sahadeva, saying "So be it," set off in that direction and then saw his brother Nakula struck down upon the ground.

sanskrit: bhrātṛśokābhisaṃtaptas tṛṣayā ca prapīḍitaḥ abhidudrāva pānīyaṃ tato vāg abhyabhāṣata
english: Scorched with grief for his brother and tormented by thirst, he rushed toward the water — and then the voice spoke to him:

sanskrit: mā tāta sāhasaṃ kārṣīr mama pūrvaparigrahaḥ praśnān uktvā yathākāmaṃ tataḥ piba harasva ca
english: "Do not act rashly, dear one — this is my prior possession. First answer my questions as you please, and then drink and take water."
